question: Was Mary free from sin?

answers.label: She was holy but had faults, like others
She was free from original sin from her conception

overview.text: Several early writers speak of Mary's faults: Tertullian counts her among the unbelieving relatives, and Chrysostom speaks of vainglory and asking at the wrong time.
Augustine, against Pelagius, excepted Mary alone from any talk of sin, for the Lord's honor. That became the common view, East and West.
In 1854 the Catholic Church defined that Mary was preserved from original sin from her conception. The Orthodox and Protestants do not accept this definition.

quotes.author: Tertullian
quotes.english: Did Christ use this saying, "Who is my mother, and who are my brothers?", fittingly, to strike at the unbelief of those standing outside, or to shake off the importunity of those calling him away from his work? ... When indignation denies parents, it does not deny them; it rebukes them.
quotes.original: indigue usus est hoc dicto ad percutiendam incredulitatem foris stantium vel ad excutiendam importunitatem ab opere revocantium? ... Cum indignatio parentes negat, non negat, sed obiurgat.
quotes.context: Against Marcion, who used the verse to deny Christ had a mother. Tertullian counts Mary among the unbelieving relatives of Mark 3:21.

quotes.author: John Chrysostom
quotes.english: So here too he healed the disease of vainglory and gave his mother the honor due to her, though she asked at the wrong time.
quotes.original: Οὕτω δὴ καὶ ἐνταῦθα τῆς τε κενοδοξίας τὸ νόσημα ἰάσατο, καὶ τὴν πρέπουσαν τιμὴν τῇ μητρὶ ἀπέδωκε, καίτοι καὶ ἄκαιρα αἰτούσῃ.
quotes.context: Chrysostom thinks Mary and the brothers wanted to show their authority over Jesus before the crowd, as at Cana. Several Greek fathers spoke of Mary's faults this way.

quotes.author: Augustine of Hippo
quotes.english: Except, then, the holy Virgin Mary, about whom, for the honor of the Lord, I want no question at all to be raised when we are dealing with sins.
quotes.original: Excepta itaque sancta virgine Maria, de qua propter honorem Domini nullam prorsus cum de peccatis agitur, haberi volo quaestionem
quotes.context: Pelagius had listed Mary among the sinless. Augustine agrees for her alone, asking how we can know what more grace she was given. He still held she was born with original sin. The Migne scan is poor here; the quote follows the standard text.

source.edition: Migne PL 44 (1845), De natura et gratia 36.42

quotes.author: Council of Trent
quotes.english: except by a special privilege from God, as the Church holds in regard of the Blessed Virgin
quotes.original: except by a special privilege from God, as the Church holds in regard of the Blessed Virgin
quotes.context: Trent says no one avoids all venial sins for a whole life except by special privilege, "as the Church holds of the Blessed Virgin".

quotes.author: Synod of Jerusalem (Orthodox)
quotes.english: and especially the Mother of God the Word, the ever-virgin Mary, did not experience these [sins], or such like faults.
quotes.original: and especially the Mother of God the Word, the ever-virgin Mary, did not experience these [sins], or such like faults.
quotes.context: The Orthodox hold Mary free of personal sin but do not accept the Immaculate Conception.

source.edition: Confession of Dositheus (Synod of Jerusalem), Decree 6 (1672)

quotes.author: Pius IX
quotes.english: the most Blessed Virgin Mary, in the first instance of her conception, by a singular grace and privilege granted by Almighty God, in view of the merits of Jesus Christ, the Savior of the human race, was preserved free from all stain of original sin
quotes.original: the most Blessed Virgin Mary, in the first instance of her conception, by a singular grace and privilege granted by Almighty God, in view of the merits of Jesus Christ, the Savior of the human race, was preserved free from all stain of original sin
quotes.context: Defined as Catholic dogma in 1854 after centuries of debate (Bernard and Aquinas questioned it; Duns Scotus defended it).

gaps.author: Origen of Alexandria
gaps.why: Simeon's sword as Mary's doubt at the cross. In the library's Luke witnesses.

gaps.author: Ephrem the Syrian
gaps.why: "You and your mother alone are wholly beautiful; no stain is in you." Syriac.

gaps.author: Irenaeus of Lyons
gaps.why: Mary as the new Eve, whose obedience untied Eve's knot.

method: Every early quote was read in its Greek or Latin and translated for this page by Claude (Opus 5.5) on 13 October 2026. Each line names the printed edition it was read from.
